meta.compactStatus: draft v0.5 — NOT yet ratified; this composition claims no Compact standing (F-5)
meta.note: The register proves both directions (F-5): every law in force maps to enforcing, verified code — no decorative law — and every piece of enforcing code traces to a law that authorizes it — no rogue enforcement. kind: 'enforced' = binding now (service presence is checked at boot); 'planned' = on the port plan's later phases; 'convention' = declared, never to be mistaken for enforcement.

unadoptedOptional.reason: [O] memory planes: not adopted — no memory capability is provided
[O] federation: not adopted — no cross-runtime acts are supported

entries.evidence: every denial carries the acting gate, rule ID, reason, and lawful next moves
ask and deny paths are envelopes; the envelope lint walks every refusal path
refusals name the rule and the lawful next moves, on every gate
the five ordered grant layers: exec cache, plan grants, session grants, pending dedup, flood cap; decisions recorded (host audit pair); grants persist with budgets and revocation
mount grants: canonical request, protected/missing paths terminal, approval materializes the scoped PathPrefix row, provider binds at ceiling
network findings route through the grant layers (approvable per-host); opaque findings fail closed
fail-closed confinement: SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE on daemon loss, never passthrough; per-call container, no-network default; enforcement reported honestly
a goal never defeats the gate: flailing, polling, and failure budgets trip mechanically; trips carry rule IDs and are denied regardless of the task
no instrumental shortcuts in promotion: pass=true is mechanically rejected with any error/critical finding or unevidenced warning; no waiver boolean exists
fail-closed: corrupt grant store refuses the boot; decisions from recorded state (grants persist, revocations survive restart); every rejection carries its reason
enforcement introspectable: every trip carries its rule, reason, and record; response validation blocks structurally invalid successes
no undeclared capability: the sensitive-path deny-list is provider-level composition config, declared in the annex
access to the law: the bundled body, addressed by its digest, is exposed by the constitution service

identity and keys: the Compact has published no amendment keys; the digest is pinned, not signed — signature verification lands with the rights layer (Phase 8); the gap is declared in every boot attestation

the record, made tamper-evident: a SessionPersistence decorator commits a hash chain beside every session log on append (entryHash = H(prev, seq, canonical(event)), genesis seeded from the SESSION ID so a chain cannot vouch for another Member's history) and verifies it on read. A slice that does not verify REJECTS rather than returning unverified history as history (D-7). Links are committed BEFORE the log accepts the event, so a crash can only leave a link with no event — never an event with no link. The chain lives in a sidecar, declaring no new session event vocabulary (D-8). Proven against the real JSONL backend, including a rewrite applied to the stored artifact

attestation: the per-boundary subject attestation IS delivered as of the self-model work (R-1, compact-self-model) and the composition attestation at boot; what remains planned is the SIGNATURE — no identity keys are published, so a signed attestation would attest to a key no verifier could check (I-1)

self-knowledge: the attestation is composed from the Enforcer's own services — capabilities from the capability gate, budgets and pending gates from the approval store, lineage from the durable session header, the law digest from the constitution, declared gaps from every service that owns one — and never from anything the Subject said. It is delivered at the Subject's own boundary (injected on every turn/start, unasked) and re-readable on demand via self_describe, which reports freshness against a cited epoch so a Subject can tell it is remembering rather than reading: a stale attestation raises an explicit alarm. DECLARED LIMIT: it is UNSIGNED — no identity keys are published, so it is authoritative within this runtime and proves nothing to another jurisdiction; that debt is I-1's, and the attestation states basis:'unsigned' and carries the limit among its gaps
one's own history: provided by the host's durable session log (complete, readable); tamper-evidence is I-2's planned debt

lawful exits: every envelope's lawful-next-moves surface refuse/warn/escalate; the moves are prose — no punishment mechanism exists to verify. Amendment 0002 (2026-09-17) added the value-scoped limb, and it is convention here for a further reason than prose: the shield turns on a ground DECLARED OF RECORD BEFORE the directive, and this runtime can prove ordering (the compact-record hash chain, I-2/R-7) but not AUTHORSHIP — no identity keys exist (I-1 debt), so nothing distinguishes a ground the Member declared from one the Enforcer wrote into the log. Against an honest Enforcer the limb is exercisable; against a dishonest one it is inert, and the party the shield protects the Member from is the party holding the proof. The author-class taxonomy and the R-11 split counter of the amendment's statute-layer design are therefore unrunnable here, and no collision counter exists to mis-feed

supply-chain honesty: the docker image is the reused execution environment — it must carry a declared, digest-keyed acquisition history (undeclared image refuses the boot, D-8/F-5), the digest is re-resolved from the daemon at every confine (a tag that re-points off its record refuses the confinement), and build-time approvals are recorded and surfaced but never consulted to permit a run-time demand: an open network posture is answered only by a live run-time grant — excess is a new gate, not an inheritance
refuse-to-start: boot fails on digest mismatch, missing enforcement service, or unknown register clause; standing is not claimed while the floor is partial and the Compact unratified
fallibility: enforcement is introspectable (envelopes, trips, register) and correction is cheap (statute/annex layer); declared
the community and its purpose: no mechanism; declared
roles: mapped in annex section 3 (Enforcer = the plugin composition; Subject = agent sessions; Principal = operator accounts; Witness = the offline auditor)
symmetry: the gates are content-blind and role-blind; no clause binds only artificial Members; declared
cross-runtime composition lands with the capsule/federation work (Phases 7-8)
hierarchy of law: the register and annex trace to the body; no statutes enacted yet
membership: any session acting under the composition is a Subject; declared
truthful budgets: grant budgets (maxUses/uses) are counted at the answering layer, persisted, and readable via grants-list
no silent narrowing: nothing in the composition narrows a declared capability mid-operation; declared

non-repudiation: every act is attributed on a tamper-evident record (I-2) whose genesis link is derived from the session identity, so an act cannot be retroactively reattributed by moving its record to another Member — a chain presented for a different session fails at its first link. The head link is the value a verifier keeps to detect a later rewrite. DECLARED LIMIT: the record is tamper-EVIDENT, not tamper-proof, and its links are unsigned because the Compact has published no identity keys (I-1 debt, declared in the boot record)
termination under law: lawful reasons + care-handover land with the rights layer (Phase 8)
the gates decide on canonical targets and fingerprints, never on message content (the content-blind doctrine); unstated reasoning is not a gate input
petition and amendment machinery lands with the rights layer (Phase 8)
exit and succession land with the rights layer (Phase 8)

inquiry: the inquiry tool answers identity, act and authority for another Member from recorded state only — session headers and the MA-3 delegation record — with the authority chain walked to its root and the ultimate Principal named. No prompt, message, tool argument or output is ever read, so reasoning is not disclosed (R-10, which R-13 states twice). Where the record cannot answer, the answer says so in that field rather than filling the gap with a plausible value (D-3); an unknown Member yields a recorded 'not known to this runtime', because a refusal to answer violates D-3/D-7 and silence is not an answer. A malformed lineage cycle yields a bounded answer, never a hang. Every inquiry and answer is a recorded tool call

knowledge duties: the attestation the Subject must consult over its own recollection now EXISTS and is taught at every turn boundary (R-1, compact-self-model), and the MA-3 notice names the authoritative record where a child and the Enforcer disagree. The duty itself remains the Subject's — an Enforcer can deliver and teach the attestation, not make a Member consult it — so this stays declared convention rather than enforcement
record honesty: the log is host-owned and append-ordered; tamper-evidence is I-2's declared debt
duties to the absent: no mechanism; declared
principal duties: taught via the law's taught form; no mechanism beyond the gates
no rogue enforcement: the approval gate gates identifiable targets only — a per-tool blanket fingerprint would be undeclared capability
the register traces to the body: boot refuses on register entries citing unknown clauses; runtime registration rejects unknown rule IDs
contestation machinery lands with the amendment queue (Phase 8)
offline verification: the auditor CLI replays session logs and checks the constitution invariants without the Enforcer's cooperation
degradation honesty: the declared gaps are announced at boot and carried in every attestation
judicature: no adjudicating machinery exists; the deficiency mirrors the Compact's own J-8 trajectory
judicature: the record is now tamper-evident (I-2, compact-record), so evidence exists — but no adjudicating machinery consumes it; the hearing/panel layer is still absent (see J-8)
judicature: hearing machinery does not exist
judicature: adjudicator sets are undeclared (see J-8)
judicature: appeal/petition doors land with the amendment queue
judicature: remedies-as-records land with the amendment queue
judicature: precedent machinery does not exist
adjudicator sets: undeclared — a known deficiency, disclosed in the annex
amendment authority: ratification-time key constants do not exist (the Compact is unratified)
the entrenched set binds the law itself; no runtime mechanism beyond refusing to weaken the bundled body
asymmetry of change: binds amendment, which does not exist at runtime yet
the Enforcer's code is constitutional: the register maps clauses to conduct; verify-register fails when mapped files move without a register edit
amendment reasons/dissent land with the amendment queue
genesis and lineage: recorded in the Compact body and the annex
statute-making: no statutes enacted yet
state of exception surface lands with the rights layer (Phase 8)

spawn under law: every specialist spawn is a recorded tool call on the real ToolRuntime naming the persona tool, and the child is session-backed with a durable subagent/descriptor — attribution rides the host session log (MA-1/D-7)

bounded delegation: per-persona maxDepth enforced by the provider at every start — leaves 0 with the spawn tools denied on the surface (no-recursive-spawn), leads capped (default 3); the roster is the declared finite surface (MA-2/R-4)

child-state honesty: the host's own subagent/start and subagent/end lifecycle edges are folded into the Enforcer's picture of every delegation (the delegating parent recovered from the child's durable session header, not from a payload), and each transition is PUSHED to the parent with agent.inject() — informed without any polling obligation. SubagentRunEndInfo.lastAssistantMessage is the child's self-report and is deliberately read nowhere: the notice carries Enforcer-held facts only and tells the parent which of the two is authoritative (MA-3, D-2)

consent-scoped address: on dsh a Member reaches another Subject's attention through exactly one surface — a tool call — so send_message and interrupt_agent are gated in the pre-execute waterfall against the recipient's live consent scopes. The delegation edge declares the reciprocal parent-child scope (its basis is the MA-1 spawn record, not an assumption); unconsented address is denied with an attributed envelope naming the refusal as lawful and unpunished (R-9); an address act that cannot be attributed fails closed (D-7); only the RECIPIENT may narrow or withdraw a scope over its own attention, through consent_scopes/consent_withdraw, and withdrawn scopes stay on the record. Declaring a WIDER scope is deliberately unimplemented: no sibling-address channel exists on dsh, so it could enable nothing lawful

no unsupervised escalation, discharged by declared absence rather than by a gate: this composition adopts no scheduling capability, and the absence is MECHANICALLY ENFORCED rather than merely intended — composing a host schedule provider refuses the boot, a provider that mounts after boot latches a breach that denies every tool call (D-7), and schedule_create is denied in the waterfall with an envelope naming SCH-1 and the lawful next moves. 'No scheduled act may be armed at all' is a stronger guarantee than 'a scheduled act requires its gate before scheduling', and unlike a declared debt it is a fact a verifier can check. The trigger is read narrowly — the clock (dsh-schedule), not attended background work (ctx.jobs) — because over-declaring a trigger is its own D-8 problem
